GEMMI (Genome and Macromolecular Models & Information) is a comprehensive C++ library for structural biology with Python bindings. It provides tools for working with macromolecular structures, electron density maps, and crystallographic data. The library specializes in handling various file formats used in structural biology, performing geometric calculations, and analyzing atomic models.

GEMMI is a joint project of [CCP4](https://www.ccp4.ac.uk/) and [Global Phasing Ltd](https://www.globalphasing.com/) [docs/index.rst:38-40](). It is written in C++14 and supports modern Python (3.9+) [pyproject.toml:13-13]().

This page provides a high-level overview of GEMMI's architecture and components. For detailed information about specific components, please refer to the child pages.

Sources: [include/gemmi/version.hpp:8-8](), [python/gemmi.cpp:162-165](), [docs/gemmi-help.txt:1-6](), [docs/index.rst:32-33]()

## Key Features

GEMMI offers a broad range of functionality for structural biology applications:

1.  **Reading and writing structural biology file formats**
    *   PDB, mmCIF, mmJSON for atomic coordinates [README.md:6-6]()
    *   MTZ, structure factor CIF for crystallographic data [README.md:8-8]()
    *   CCP4/MRC and other formats for electron density maps [README.md:9-9]()
2.  **Macromolecular structure manipulation**
    *   Traversing and modifying atomic models (Structure → Model → Chain → Residue → Atom) [include/gemmi/model.hpp:119-918]()
    *   Handling of alternative conformations and microheterogeneity [include/gemmi/model.hpp:124-124]()
3.  **Crystallographic computations**
    *   Structure factor calculation and Fourier transforms [docs/gemmi-help.txt:37-38]()
    *   Symmetry operations and space group handling [docs/gemmi-help.txt:39-39]()
    *   Unit cell calculations and coordinate transformations [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:24-40]()
4.  **Accessibility options**
    *   Python bindings via `nanobind` for easy scripting [python/common.h:11-24]()
    *   Command-line interface (`gemmi` executable) for common tasks [docs/gemmi-help.txt:8-45]()
    *   WebAssembly (WASM) bindings for browser-based tools [docs/install.rst:171-180]()

For a full summary of capabilities, see [Key Features](#1.1).

Sources: [README.md:4-11](), [docs/gemmi-help.txt:10-45](), [docs/index.rst:13-21]()

## System Architecture

GEMMI is designed as a C++ library with multiple interface layers. While it was originally header-only, it now includes a compiled core library `libgemmi_cpp` for performance and modularity [docs/install.rst:10-20]().

### High-Level Component Diagram

This diagram maps the natural language concepts of the system to their primary code entities.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Core Library (C++14)"
        [Structure] --> [Symmetry]
        [Structure] --> [UnitCell]
        [CIF_Parser] --> [Structure]
        [MTZ_Handler] --> [Reflection_Data]
        [Grid_System] --> [CCP4_Map]
    end
    
    subgraph "Interfaces"
        CLI["gemmi executable (prog/)"]
        PyAPI["gemmi_ext (python/)"]
        WASM["WebAssembly (wasm/)"]
        Fortran["Fortran Bindings (fortran/)"]
    end
    
    [Structure] -.-> |"wrapped by"| PyAPI
    [Structure] -.-> |"used by"| CLI
    [Grid_System] -.-> |"wrapped by"| PyAPI
    [MTZ_Handler] -.-> |"exposed to"| WASM
    [Structure] -.-> |"linked to"| Fortran
```

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:21-28](), [python/common.h:27-49](), [docs/install.rst:10-20](), [docs/install.rst:147-154]()

### Data Flow Architecture

The following diagram illustrates the flow of data from external files through Gemmi's internal classes to final outputs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input Files"
        PDB_File[".pdb"]
        CIF_File[".cif / .mmcif"]
        MTZ_File[".mtz"]
        Map_File[".ccp4 / .mrc"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Classes"
        Structure["gemmi::Structure"]
        Document["gemmi::cif::Document"]
        Mtz["gemmi::Mtz"]
        Grid["gemmi::Grid"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Outputs"
        JSON[".json"]
        Validation["Validation Reports"]
        Calculated_Map["Electron Density"]
    end
    
    PDB_File --> |"read_pdb()"| Structure
    CIF_File --> |"read_structure()"| Structure
    CIF_File --> |"cif::read()"| Document
    MTZ_File --> |"read_mtz_file()"| Mtz
    Map_File --> |"read_ccp4_map()"| Grid
    
    Structure --> |"gemmi convert"| JSON
    Structure --> |"gemmi validate"| Validation
    Mtz --> |"gemmi sf2map"| Calculated_Map
    Grid --> |"gemmi map"| Calculated_Map
```

Sources: [docs/gemmi-help.txt:10-45](), [python/common.h:34-40](), [docs/install.rst:184-196]()

For technical details on the build system and binding internals, see [Architecture Overview](#1.2).

## Core Data Structures

GEMMI's functionality is built around several key data structures. The central structure is the hierarchy representing macromolecular models.

### Structure Hierarchy

The structural hierarchy follows the standard PDB model:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Structure {
        +vector~Model~ models
        +UnitCell cell
        +SpaceGroup spacegroup
    }
    class Model {
        +vector~Chain~ chains
    }
    class Chain {
        +vector~Residue~ residues
        +string name
    }
    class Residue {
        +vector~Atom~ atoms
        +SeqId seqid
    }
    class Atom {
        +Position pos
        +float occ
        +float b_iso
        +Element element
    }
    Structure "1" *-- "many" Model
    Model "1" *-- "many" Chain
    Chain "1" *-- "many" Residue
    Residue "1" *-- "many" Atom
```

Sources: [include/gemmi/model.hpp:119-164](), [include/gemmi/model.hpp:183-225](), [include/gemmi/model.hpp:482-572](), [include/gemmi/model.hpp:718-750](), [include/gemmi/model.hpp:883-918]()

### Summary of Key Classes

| Category | Class | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Coordinates** | `gemmi::Structure` | Root object for macromolecular models [include/gemmi/model.hpp:883]() |
| **Symmetry** | `gemmi::SpaceGroup` | Space group information and operations [python/common.h:29]() |
| **Grid/Maps** | `gemmi::Grid` | 3D volumetric data storage [python/common.h:31]() |
| **Reflections** | `gemmi::Mtz` | MTZ reflection data file handling [python/common.h:37]() |
| **CIF** | `gemmi::cif::Document` | DOM-like representation of a CIF file [python/common.h:38]() |

Sources: [python/common.h:25-49](), [include/gemmi/model.hpp:883-918]()

## User Interfaces

### Command Line Interface (CLI)
The `gemmi` program provides subcommands for common structural biology tasks such as `convert`, `validate`, `mtz`, and `sfcalc` [docs/gemmi-help.txt:10-45]().

### Python API
The Python module `gemmi` (and its extension `gemmi_ext`) allows users to manipulate structures and data using NumPy-friendly interfaces [python/gemmi.cpp:159-165](). It uses `nanobind` for efficient C++/Python interop [pyproject.toml:4-4]().

For details on the CLI, see [Command Line Interface](#6). For Python usage, see [Python API](#7).

Sources: [docs/gemmi-help.txt:1-45](), [python/gemmi.cpp:159-185](), [pyproject.toml:1-7]()

GEMMI (Genome and Macromolecular Models & Information) is a comprehensive library for structural biology with a focus on crystallography and macromolecular structures. This page summarizes the main capabilities and features of the library, providing an overview of its core components, file format support, and programming interfaces.

## Core Data Structures

Gemmi is built around several fundamental data structures that form the basis for all other functionality.

### Macromolecular Structure Representation

The `Structure` system provides a complete hierarchical representation of macromolecular structures, following the standard organization found in PDB/mmCIF files. It uses a specialized container system to manage models, chains, residues, and atoms.

**Bridge: Natural Language to Code Entity Space (Molecular Hierarchy)**

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "gemmi::Structure Hierarchy"
        Structure["class Structure [include/gemmi/model.hpp]"]
        Model["struct Model [include/gemmi/model.hpp]"]
        Chain["struct Chain [include/gemmi/model.hpp]"]
        Residue["struct Residue [include/gemmi/model.hpp]"]
        Atom["struct Atom [include/gemmi/model.hpp]"]
        
        Structure -- "std::vector<Model> models" --> Model
        Model -- "std::vector<Chain> chains" --> Chain
        Chain -- "std::vector<Residue> residues" --> Residue
        Residue -- "std::vector<Atom> atoms" --> Atom
    end

    subgraph "Metadata & Context"
        UnitCell["class UnitCell [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp]"]
        SpaceGroup["struct SpaceGroup [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp]"]
        Entity["struct Entity [include/gemmi/metadata.hpp]"]
        Connection["struct Connection [include/gemmi/metadata.hpp]"]
        
        Structure -- "cell" --> UnitCell
        Structure -- "find_spacegroup()" --> SpaceGroup
        Structure -- "entities" --> Entity
        Structure -- "connections" --> Connection
    end
```
Sources: [include/gemmi/model.hpp:136-222](), [include/gemmi/model.hpp:882-1056](), [python/mol.cpp:132-154](), [docs/mol.rst:8-18]()

The `Structure` class is the root container. Key features include:
- **Models**: Supports multiple alternative models (e.g., from NMR or different refinement runs) [include/gemmi/model.hpp:886]().
- **Alternative Conformations**: Handles `altloc` at the `Atom` level [include/gemmi/model.hpp:139]() and provides `AtomGroup`/`ResidueGroup` proxies for grouping alternatives [include/gemmi/model.hpp:184-200]().
- **Crystallographic Context**: Stores `UnitCell` for coordinate transformations and `SpaceGroup` for symmetry [include/gemmi/model.hpp:891-893]().

### 3D Volumetric Data Representation

The Grid system provides a framework for handling 3D volumetric data, such as electron density maps, using the `Grid` template class.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Grid System Entities"
        GridT["template Grid<T> [include/gemmi/grid.hpp]"]
        FloatGrid["using FloatGrid = Grid<float>"]
        Int8Grid["using Int8Grid = Grid<int8_t>"]
        Ccp4["struct Ccp4 [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp]"]
        
        Ccp4 -- "contains" --> FloatGrid
    end
    
    subgraph "Operations"
        Interpolate["interpolate_value()"]
        Symmetrize["symmetrize_max()"]
        Mask["class SolvMasker [include/gemmi/solmask.hpp]"]
        
        GridT --- Interpolate
        GridT --- Symmetrize
        GridT --- Mask
    end
```
Sources: [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:311-565](), [python/grid.cpp:77-150](), [docs/grid.rst:7-32]()

## File Format Support

Gemmi supports a wide array of crystallographic and structural formats through specialized parsers and writers.

### Coordinate and Chemical Formats
- **mmCIF (PDBx/mmCIF)**: Primary format, handled via `populate_structure_from_block` [include/gemmi/mmcif.hpp:16]().
- **PDB**: Legacy format support including Hybrid-36 serial numbers and large chain ID extensions [include/gemmi/pdb.hpp:7-11]().
- **mmJSON**: JSON representation of macromolecular data [python/mol.cpp:99]().
- **ChemComp**: Reading from Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) or Monomer Library [include/gemmi/mmcif.hpp:39-44]().

### Reflection and Map Formats
- **MTZ**: Standard binary format for reflections, managed by the `Mtz` class [python/mtz.cpp:79]().
- **CCP4 Maps**: Volumetric data format for electron density [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp]().
- **XDS**: Support for `XDS_ASCII` conversion to MTZ [docs/gemmi-help.txt:44]().

**Bridge: Natural Language to Code Entity Space (I/O Operations)**

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["File on Disk"] -- "read_structure()" --> Structure["gemmi::Structure"]
    Structure -- "write_pdb()" --> PDBOut["PDB File"]
    Structure -- "make_mmcif_document()" --> CIFOut["cif::Document"]
    
    ReflFile["MTZ File"] -- "read_mtz_file()" --> MtzObj["gemmi::Mtz"]
    MtzObj -- "write_mtz()" --> ReflOut["MTZ File"]

    click Structure "[include/gemmi/model.hpp]"
    click MtzObj "[include/gemmi/mtz.hpp]"
```
Sources: [include/gemmi/pdb.hpp:34-60](), [include/gemmi/mmcif.hpp:16-30](), [include/gemmi/to_pdb.hpp:51-61](), [include/gemmi/to_mmcif.hpp:58-71](), [docs/mol.rst:105-124]()

## Advanced Crystallographic Tools

### Symmetry and Unit Cells
Gemmi implements sophisticated symmetry handling:
- **Space Groups**: Lookup by H-M name, Hall symbol, or number [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp]().
- **Operations**: `Op` class for 3x3 matrices and translation vectors [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp]().
- **Niggli Reduction**: Lattice reduction tools in `unitcell.hpp`.

### Chemical Analysis and Refinement
- **Neighbor Search**: Uses `NeighborSearch` and `SubCells` for fast spatial queries [docs/gemmi-help.txt:16]().
- **Topology**: The `crd` command prepares topology for Refmac [docs/gemmi-help.txt:19]().
- **Restraints**: `AceDrg` integration for filling restraint values [docs/gemmi-help.txt:20]().

## Programming Interfaces

### C++ Library
A header-only core (with some optional compiled components) providing high-performance primitives. It requires C++11 or later [include/gemmi/version.hpp]().

### Python Bindings
Gemmi provides extensive Python bindings using `nanobind`. These bindings are designed for performance, often providing direct access to C++ memory via NumPy [python/mol.cpp:1-20]().
- **NumPy Integration**: Grids and reflection data can be viewed as NumPy arrays.
- **Ease of Use**: Functions like `gemmi.read_structure()` handle format detection and decompression (`.gz`) automatically [docs/mol.rst:188-194]().

### Command Line Interface (CLI)
The `gemmi` executable provides a suite of subcommands for common tasks:
- `convert`: Format conversion (e.g., mmCIF to PDB) [docs/gemmi-help.txt:18]().
- `mtz2cif` / `cif2mtz`: Reflection data conversion [docs/gemmi-help.txt:14,32]().
- `sfcalc`: Structure factor calculation from models [docs/gemmi-help.txt:38]().
- `blobs`: Unmodeled density detection [docs/gemmi-help.txt:12]().

Sources: [docs/gemmi-help.txt:1-45](), [python/mol.cpp:74-128](), [run-tests.sh:5-10]()

This document describes the high-level architecture of the GEMMI (Genome and Macromolecular Models & Information) library, explaining the main components and how they interact. GEMMI is a comprehensive library for structural biology, providing tools for working with atomic models, electron density maps, crystallographic symmetry, and crystallographic data.

## Core Architecture

GEMMI is organized as a layered architecture. The core logic is implemented in C++ as a header-only library, supplemented by a compiled C++ library for heavier operations, Python bindings via `nanobind`, and WebAssembly (WASM) interfaces via `embind`.

| Component | Implementation | Primary Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Header-only Core** | C++ (`include/gemmi/*.hpp`) | High-performance crystallographic math, symmetry, and data structures. |
| **Compiled Library** | C++ (`src/*.cpp`) | Heavier I/O, complex algorithms, and shared symbols for bindings. |
| **Python Bindings** | C++ / `nanobind` (`python/`) | High-level scripting interface with NumPy integration. |
| **CLI Tools** | C++ (`prog/`) | Standalone utilities like `gemmi mtz2cif` or `gemmi contact`. |
| **WASM Bindings** | C++ / `embind` (`wasm/`) | Browser-based execution for molecular viewers and web tools. |

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:21-29](), [python/gemmi.cpp:159-165](), [wasm/Makefile:15-26]()

### High-Level Component Interaction

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Foundation Layer"
        UnitCell["Unit Cell & Transforms"]
        Symmetry["Crystallographic Symmetry"]
        CIF["CIF Parser"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Data Structures"
        Structure["Structure System<br>Structure→Model→Chain→Residue→Atom"]
        Grid["Grid & Map System"]
        Refl["Reflection Data"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Interfaces"
        Python["Python (nanobind)"]
        CLI["CLI (gemmi prog)"]
        WASM["WebAssembly (embind)"]
        Fortran["Fortran (SHROUD)"]
    end
    
    UnitCell --> Structure
    UnitCell --> Grid
    UnitCell --> Refl
    
    Symmetry --> Structure
    Symmetry --> Grid
    Symmetry --> Refl
    
    CIF --> Structure
    Refl --> WASM
    Structure --> Python
    Grid --> Python
    Refl --> Python
    
    Structure --> CLI
    Grid --> CLI
    Refl --> CLI
```

Sources: [include/gemmi/model.hpp:1-1056](), [python/common.h:27-48](), [wasm/common.h:7-11](), [CMakeLists.txt:21-25]()

## Structure System

The `Structure` system represents macromolecular data hierarchically. In C++, this is defined in `include/gemmi/model.hpp`. The WASM interface maps these to JavaScript classes using `embind`.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Structure {
        +UnitCell cell
        +vector~Model~ models
        +vector~Connection~ connections
    }
    class Model {
        +int num
        +vector~Chain~ chains
        +count_occupancies()
    }
    class Chain {
        +string name
        +vector~Residue~ residues
    }
    class Residue {
        +ResidueId name
        +vector~Atom~ atoms
        +ResidueSs ss_from_file
    }
    class Atom {
        +Position pos
        +float occ
        +float b_iso
        +Element element
    }
    Structure "1" *-- "*" Model
    Model "1" *-- "*" Chain
    Chain "1" *-- "*" Residue
    Residue "1" *-- "*" Atom
```

In the WASM implementation, the hierarchy is exposed through `at()` methods and `length` properties to facilitate efficient traversal in JavaScript environments.

Sources: [wasm/gemmi.d.ts:56-108](), [wasm/mol.cpp:40-56](), [include/gemmi/model.hpp:883-1056]()

## Python Bindings via Nanobind

The Python bindings use `nanobind` to bridge C++ entities to Python. The implementation is modular, with specialized `add_*` functions for different domains.

| Function | Source File | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `add_mol` | `python/mol.cpp` | Binds `Structure`, `Model`, `Chain`, etc. |
| `add_grid` | `python/grid.cpp` | Binds 3D density grids and NumPy integration. |
| `add_mtz` | `python/mtz.cpp` | Binds MTZ reflection data reading/writing. |
| `add_cif` | `python/cif.cpp` | Binds the CIF DOM (Document, Block, Table). |

The bindings also include specialized logic for Pythonic indexing and NumPy array views. For example, `normalize_index` handles negative indices in Python lists.

Sources: [python/common.h:27-48](), [python/common.h:69-72](), [python/gemmi.cpp:159-180]()

## WebAssembly (WASM) Architecture

The WASM build uses Emscripten to compile a subset of the C++ library for use in browsers. It includes a custom `BondInfo` and `SelectionResult` system to optimize data transfer between the WASM heap and JavaScript.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant JS as JavaScript
    participant WASM as Gemmi WASM
    participant Heap as WASM Heap (Memory)

    JS->>WASM: read_structure(buffer, name)
    WASM->>Heap: Allocate Structure
    WASM-->>JS: Return Structure Handle
    JS->>WASM: BondInfo.get_bond_lines(structure)
    WASM->>Heap: Compute bonds & store in int32_t vector
    JS->>WASM: bond_data_ptr()
    WASM-->>JS: Memory Address (uintptr_t)
    JS->>Heap: Read typed array from address
```

Key WASM components:
- **`MtzFft`**: Performs Fast Fourier Transforms on MTZ data to generate maps directly in the browser.
- **`Isosurface`**: Extracts mesh data (vertices/triangles) from grids for 3D visualization.
- **`BondInfo`**: Uses the `MonLib` (Monomer Library) to calculate connectivity for visualization.

Sources: [wasm/mol.cpp:110-178](), [wasm/mtz_fft.cpp:119-198](), [wasm/gemmi.d.ts:148-174](), [wasm/Makefile:15-26]()

## Build System and Integration

Gemmi uses CMake as its primary build system. It is designed to be flexible, supporting standalone builds, `scikit-build-core` for Python wheels, and Emscripten for WASM.

- **`gemmi_headers`**: An INTERFACE target for the header-only core.
- **`gemmi_cpp`**: The compiled library containing non-templated code and third-party dependencies (e.g., `zlib`, `pocketfft`).
- **`gemmi_ext`**: The Python extension module created via `nanobind_add_module`.

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:21-29](), [CMakeLists.txt:121-164](), [python/gemmi.cpp:159-162]()

## Data Flow: Reflection to Map

A common architectural pattern in Gemmi is the transformation of reciprocal space data (reflections) to real space data (grids/maps).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Reciprocal Space"
        MTZ["gemmi::Mtz"]
        Proxy["gemmi::MtzExternalDataProxy"]
        FPhi["gemmi::FPhiProxy"]
    end

    subgraph "Processing"
        FFT["gemmi::get_f_phi_on_grid"]
        Trans["gemmi::transform_f_phi_grid_to_map_"]
    end

    subgraph "Real Space"
        Grid["gemmi::Grid<float>"]
        Stats["gemmi::calculate_data_statistics"]
    end

    MTZ --> Proxy
    Proxy --> FPhi
    FPhi --> FFT
    FFT --> Trans
    Trans --> Grid
    Grid --> Stats
```

This flow is utilized in both the Python `sf` module and the WASM `mtz_fft` module to generate electron density maps for visualization or refinement.

Sources: [wasm/mtz_fft.cpp:29-60](), [python/common.h:48](), [include/gemmi/fourier.hpp:1-50]()

- [docs/install.rst](docs/install.rst)
- [docs/misc.rst](docs/misc.rst)
- [docs/wcn-help.txt](docs/wcn-help.txt)
- [python/common.h](python/common.h)
- [python/gemmi.cpp](python/gemmi.cpp)

</details>



This page covers the installation and configuration of the Gemmi library, a comprehensive toolkit for structural biology and crystallography. Instructions are provided for different installation methods, platform-specific considerations, and configuration options.

For information about using Gemmi after installation, see the [Core Data Structures](#3) and [Command Line Interface](#6) documentation.

## Installation Methods Overview

Gemmi can be installed in multiple ways, depending on your needs:

1.  **Python package** - Install through pip (Python bindings only).
2.  **Build from source** - Full installation with C++ library, command-line tools, and optional Python/Fortran bindings.
3.  **Conda** - Available via `conda-forge`.
4.  **CCP4 Suite** - Included in standard CCP4 distributions.

### Component Relationship Diagram

The following diagram maps high-level installation targets to their corresponding code entities and build artifacts.

**Gemmi Build Artifact Mapping**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Build Targets"
        direction TB
        T_HEADERS["gemmi_headers [INTERFACE]"]
        T_CPP["gemmi_cpp [STATIC/SHARED]"]
        T_PROG["gemmi_prog [EXECUTABLE]"]
        T_PY["gemmi_py [MODULE]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Source Entities"
        direction TB
        S_CORE["include/gemmi/*.hpp"]
        S_CLI["src/main.cpp"]
        S_PY["python/gemmi.cpp"]
    end

    subgraph "Installation Output"
        direction TB
        OUT_BIN["gemmi binary"]
        OUT_SO["libgemmi_cpp.so / .dll"]
        OUT_PY["gemmi_ext.so / .pyd"]
    end

    S_CORE --> T_HEADERS
    T_HEADERS --> T_CPP
    S_CLI --> T_PROG
    S_PY --> T_PY
    
    T_PROG --> OUT_BIN
    T_CPP --> OUT_SO
    T_PY --> OUT_PY
```
Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:21-32](), [CMakeLists.txt:217-221](), [CMakeLists.txt:268-270](), [docs/install.rst:46-56]()

## System Requirements

### Core Requirements
- **C++14 compatible compiler**: Minimum requirement for the core library [docs/install.rst:55-56]().
- **C++17 compatible compiler**: Required if building Python bindings from source [docs/install.rst:94-95]().
- **CMake 3.15 or newer**: Required for the build system [CMakeLists.txt:1-1]().

### Python Bindings Requirements
- **Python 3.8 or newer** [docs/install.rst:96-96]().
- **nanobind**: Used for generating high-performance bindings [python/common.h:11-11]().
- **scikit-build-core**: Used for pip-based source builds [docs/install.rst:128-128]().

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:1-10](), [docs/install.rst:7-100](), [python/common.h:20-22]()

## Python Installation

The simplest way to install the Gemmi Python module is via `pip`.

### From PyPI
```bash
pip install gemmi
```
This typically downloads binary wheels. If no wheel matches, it compiles from source using `scikit-build-core` [docs/install.rst:86-95]().

### From Source (Git)
```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/project-gemmi/gemmi.git
```
You can pass CMake arguments during pip installation:
```bash
pip install . --config-settings="cmake.args=-DFETCH_ZLIB_NG=ON"
```
Sources: [docs/install.rst:118-136](), [CMakeLists.txt:14-19]()

For more details, see [Python Installation](#2.2).

## Building from Source

Building from source provides access to the C++ library and the `gemmi` command-line utility.

### Basic Build Process
1. **Configure**: `cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`
2. **Build**: `cmake --build build -j4`
3. **Install**: `cmake --install build`

### Build Configuration Options

Gemmi uses several CMake options to manage dependencies and features:

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS` | ON | Build shared library [CMakeLists.txt:21]() |
| `BUILD_GEMMI_PROGRAM` | ON | Build `gemmi` command-line tool [CMakeLists.txt:22]() |
| `USE_PYTHON` | OFF | Build Python bindings [CMakeLists.txt:25]() |
| `USE_ZLIB_NG` | OFF | Use system `zlib-ng` [CMakeLists.txt:26]() |
| `FETCH_ZLIB_NG` | OFF | Download and build `zlib-ng` statically [CMakeLists.txt:27]() |
| `INTERNAL_ZLIB` | OFF | Use bundled `zlib` subset [CMakeLists.txt:28]() |
| `USE_FORTRAN` | OFF | Build Fortran bindings (experimental) [CMakeLists.txt:24]() |

### Dependency Management (zlib)
Gemmi can handle `zlib` in four ways, prioritized by CMake logic:
1. `FETCH_ZLIB_NG`: Downloads `zlib-ng` from GitHub [CMakeLists.txt:121-152]().
2. `USE_ZLIB_NG`: Searches for a system-installed `zlib-ng` [CMakeLists.txt:153-155]().
3. `INTERNAL_ZLIB`: Uses code in `third_party/zlib` [CMakeLists.txt:157-164]().
4. Default: Searches for system `zlib`; falls back to `third_party/zlib` if not found [docs/install.rst:66-67]().

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:21-32](), [CMakeLists.txt:121-164](), [docs/install.rst:58-72]()

For more details, see [Building from Source](#2.1).

## Platform-Specific Considerations

### Windows
- **Unicode**: Use `-DUSE_WMAIN=ON` (default) to enable Unicode argument support in the command-line program [CMakeLists.txt:31-32]().
- **DLLs**: When linking against `zlib` DLLs, the DLL must be in the same directory as the executable. Static linking via `-DFETCH_ZLIB_NG=ON` is recommended [docs/install.rst:69-72]().

### WebAssembly (WASM)
Gemmi can be compiled with Emscripten. The project provides two paths:
1. **Embind**: Exposes C++ classes like `Structure` and `Mtz` to JavaScript [docs/install.rst:183-197]().
2. **C API**: Used for high-performance web tools in the separate `wasm` repository [docs/install.rst:203-214]().

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:31-32](), [docs/install.rst:75-77](), [docs/install.rst:171-214]()

## Verifying Installation

### Command-Line Interface
Check the version of the installed `gemmi` utility:
```bash
gemmi --version
```
Sources: [docs/gemmi-help.txt:6-6]()

### Python Module
Verify the module and version:
```python
import gemmi
print(gemmi.__version__)
```
Sources: [python/gemmi.cpp:165-165]()

## Installation Architecture

The following diagram illustrates how the build system connects source files to the final installed environment.

**Gemmi Installation Flow**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Source Root"
        INC["include/gemmi/"]
        SRC["src/"]
        PY["python/"]
        EXT["third_party/"]
    end

    subgraph "CMake Build"
        direction TB
        CM["CMakeLists.txt"]
        ZLIB{"zlib source?"}
    end

    subgraph "Installation Paths"
        direction TB
        LIB_DIR["${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}"]
        BIN_DIR["${CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR}"]
        INC_DIR["${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}/gemmi"]
    end

    INC --> INC_DIR
    SRC --> CM
    PY --> CM
    EXT --> ZLIB
    ZLIB --> CM
    
    CM --> BIN_DIR
    CM --> LIB_DIR
```
Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:12-19](), [CMakeLists.txt:121-164](), [docs/install.rst:19-56]()

# Page: Building from Source

# Building from Source

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.appveyor.yml](.appveyor.yml)
- [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml)
- [.github/workflows/testwheel.yml](.github/workflows/testwheel.yml)
- [CMakeLists.txt](CMakeLists.txt)
- [python/common.h](python/common.h)
- [python/gemmi.cpp](python/gemmi.cpp)

</details>



This document explains how to build the GEMMI (Genome and Macromolecular Models & Information) library from source code. If you're only interested in installing the Python package, see [Python Installation](2.2).

## Prerequisites

To build GEMMI from source, you need:

- C++ compiler with C++14 support (GCC 5+, Clang 3.4+, MSVC 2019+) [CMakeLists.txt:52]()
- CMake 3.15 or newer [CMakeLists.txt:1]()
- (Optional) Python 3.9+ with development headers for Python bindings [python/common.h:20-22]()
- (Optional) zlib or zlib-ng development files [CMakeLists.txt:153-164]()

## Build Process Overview

GEMMI uses CMake as its build system. The build process consists of the following main steps:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Clone Repository"] --> B["Configure with CMake"]
    B --> C["Build with CMake"]
    C --> D["Run Tests (Optional)"]
    D --> E["Install Library"]
```

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:1-10](), [.github/workflows/ci.yml:45-58]()

## Basic Usage

### Getting the Source Code

Clone the repository from GitHub:

```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/project-gemmi/gemmi.git
cd gemmi
```

### Configuring and Building

Create a build directory and run CMake configuration:

```bash
mkdir build
cd build
cmake ..
```

Then build the project:

```bash
cmake --build . -j 4
```

To install:

```bash
sudo cmake --install .
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:45-58](), [.github/workflows/ci.yml:134-144]()

## Build Configuration Options

GEMMI offers many configuration options through CMake. Here are the most important ones:

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS` | ON | Build shared library instead of static [CMakeLists.txt:21]() |
| `BUILD_GEMMI_PROGRAM` | ON | Build the `gemmi` command-line program [CMakeLists.txt:22]() |
| `INSTALL_DEV_FILES` | ON | Install C++ headers, CMake configs, static lib [CMakeLists.txt:23]() |
| `USE_PYTHON` | OFF | Build Python bindings [CMakeLists.txt:25]() |
| `USE_FORTRAN` | OFF | Build Fortran bindings [CMakeLists.txt:24]() |
| `USE_ZLIB_NG` | OFF | Use `zlib-ng` instead of `zlib` [CMakeLists.txt:26]() |
| `FETCH_ZLIB_NG` | OFF | Download and build `zlib-ng` statically [CMakeLists.txt:27]() |
| `INTERNAL_ZLIB` | OFF | Use subset of zlib distributed with gemmi [CMakeLists.txt:28]() |
| `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` | Release | Build type (Debug, Release, MinSizeRel, RelWithDebInfo) [CMakeLists.txt:115-118]() |

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:21-43](), [CMakeLists.txt:115-118]()

## Library Components and Targets

The build system defines several targets that represent different layers of the library.

### Code Entity Relationship

The following diagram maps CMake targets to the source entities they encompass:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Target: gemmi_headers"
        H["include/gemmi/*.hpp"]
    end

    subgraph "Target: gemmi_cpp"
        L["libgemmi_cpp.so / .dll"]
    end

    subgraph "Target: gemmi_prog"
        P["gemmi (executable)"]
    end

    subgraph "Target: gemmi_py"
        PY["gemmi_ext (Python Module)"]
    end

    H -->|INTERFACE| L
    L -->|LINK| P
    L -->|LINK| PY
    
    style H stroke-dasharray: 5 5
```

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:206-212](), [CMakeLists.txt:214-223](), [CMakeLists.txt:324-342](), [CMakeLists.txt:471-479]()

## Dependency Management

### Zlib and Zlib-ng
GEMMI requires zlib for handling compressed files (e.g., `.gz` structures or MTZ files). It supports three modes:
1. **System Zlib**: Found via `find_package(ZLIB)` [CMakeLists.txt:159]().
2. **Internal Zlib**: Uses a bundled subset in `third_party/zlib` [CMakeLists.txt:162]().
3. **Zlib-ng**: A performance-optimized version. Can be used if already installed (`USE_ZLIB_NG`) or fetched automatically during build (`FETCH_ZLIB_NG`) [CMakeLists.txt:121-155]().

### Python Bindings (nanobind)
The Python bindings require `nanobind`. If `USE_PYTHON` is enabled, CMake searches for the `nanobind` package or expects it to be available in the environment [python/common.h:11]().

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:121-164](), [python/common.h:11-25]()

## Platform-Specific Instructions

### Linux
Standard GCC/Clang builds. Ensure `libz-dev` is installed for system zlib support [.github/workflows/ci.yml:130]().

### macOS
Supports both Intel and Apple Silicon. Uses `AppleClang` by default [.github/workflows/ci.yml:7-18]().

### Windows
Supports MSVC (Visual Studio 2019/2022) and MinGW. 
- For MSVC: `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64` [.appveyor.yml:6-9]().
- For Unicode support in the CLI: `USE_WMAIN` is ON by default [CMakeLists.txt:31]().

Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:130](), [.appveyor.yml:6-26](), [CMakeLists.txt:31-33]()

## Building Python Bindings

The Python module `gemmi_ext` is built using `nanobind` and links against `libgemmi_cpp`.

### Module Structure

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "python/ directory"
        G_CPP["gemmi.cpp (Entry Point)"]
        C_H["common.h (Header)"]
        M_CPP["mol.cpp"]
        S_CPP["sym.cpp"]
    end

    G_CPP -->|includes| C_H
    G_CPP -->|defines| NB_MOD["NB_MODULE(gemmi_ext, m)"]
    C_H -->|declares| ADD_FUNCS["add_mol(), add_symmetry(), etc."]
```

The `NB_MODULE` macro in `python/gemmi.cpp` initializes the extension and imports the base `gemmi` Python package to inject C++ classes [python/gemmi.cpp:159-165]().

Sources: [python/gemmi.cpp:159-180](), [python/common.h:27-48]()

## Testing the Build

GEMMI includes a comprehensive test suite accessible via CMake:

```bash
# Run all tests
cmake --build . --target check
# Or via ctest
ctest --output-on-failure
```

Python tests can be run independently:
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -v -s tests/
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:54](), [.github/workflows/ci.yml:61-62](), [.github/workflows/ci.yml:143-145]()

# Python Installation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)

- [tools/release.txt](tools/release.txt)

This document explains how to install and use the Python bindings for Gemmi. Python bindings allow you to use Gemmi's functionality directly from Python programs, leveraging `nanobind` for efficient C++/Python interoperation.

## Pre-built Wheels Installation

The simplest way to install Gemmi is using `pip` with pre-built wheels:

```bash
pip install gemmi
```

This automatically fetches and installs the appropriate binary package for your platform from PyPI. Gemmi currently supports Python 3.9 and newer [pyproject.toml:13]().

For development versions, you can install directly from GitHub:

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/project-gemmi/gemmi.git
```

Sources: [pyproject.toml:10-13](), [tools/release.txt:13-20]()

## Installation Architecture

Gemmi uses `scikit-build-core` as the build backend to bridge the Python packaging ecosystem with the CMake build system.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Natural Language: Installation Methods"
        PyPI["PyPI Install<br>(pip install gemmi)"]
        SourcePip["Source Install via pip<br>(pip install .)"]
        SourceCMake["Manual CMake Build<br>(cmake -D USE_PYTHON=ON)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Code Entity Space: Build Backend"
        scikit["scikit-build-core<br>(pyproject.toml:7)"]
        nanobind["nanobind >= 2.4<br>(pyproject.toml:4)"]
        CMake["CMakeLists.txt"]
        CppCompiler["C++ Compiler"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Code Entity Space: Artifacts"
        PythonModule["gemmi/__init__.py"]
        ExtensionModule["gemmi_ext<br>(python/gemmi.cpp:159)"]
        TypeStubs["*.pyi files<br>(CMakeLists.txt:29)"]
    end
    
    PyPI -->|"Pre-built wheel"| PythonModule
    SourcePip -->|"Uses"| scikit
    scikit -->|"Configures"| CMake
    SourceCMake -->|"Direct configuration"| CMake
    CMake -->|"Uses"| nanobind
    CMake -->|"Invokes"| CppCompiler
    CppCompiler -->|"Builds"| ExtensionModule
    CppCompiler -->|"Generates"| TypeStubs
    ExtensionModule -->|"Imported by"| PythonModule
```

Sources: [pyproject.toml:1-7](), [CMakeLists.txt:14-19](), [python/gemmi.cpp:159-162]()

## Building from Source using pip

You can build Gemmi from source using `pip`, which requires:

- C++17 compiler (required for full support, especially on macOS [pyproject.toml:99-100]())
- Python 3.9 or later [pyproject.toml:13]()
- CMake 3.15 or later [CMakeLists.txt:1]()

To install from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/project-gemmi/gemmi.git
cd gemmi
pip install .
```

This uses `scikit-build-core` to handle the `pyproject.toml` configuration, which defines `USE_PYTHON="ON"` and `GENERATE_STUBS="ON"` by default during the build process [pyproject.toml:74-77]().

Sources: [pyproject.toml:1-13](), [pyproject.toml:74-77](), [CMakeLists.txt:1-9]()

## Building from Source using CMake

For more control, you can use CMake directly. The `USE_PYTHON` option must be enabled:

```bash
cmake -D USE_PYTHON=ON ..
make gemmi_py
```

The `gemmi_py` target specifically builds the Python bindings [run-tests.sh:31-34](). If `Python_EXECUTABLE` is defined and `SKBUILD` is not (manual build), `USE_PYTHON` is forced to `ON` [CMakeLists.txt:56-58]().

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:25](), [CMakeLists.txt:56-59](), [run-tests.sh:31-34]()

## Module Structure

The Python package is structured as a hybrid of Python code and a compiled C++ extension.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language: Python Package"
        gemmi_pkg["gemmi (Python Package)"]
        gemmi_ext["gemmi_ext (C++ Extension)"]
        cif_mod["gemmi.cif (Submodule)"]
        stubs["Type Stubs (.pyi)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Code Entity Space: Implementation"
        ext_def["NB_MODULE(gemmi_ext, m_)"]
        common_h["python/common.h"]
        gemmi_cpp["python/gemmi.cpp"]
        init_py["python/gemmi/__init__.py"]
    end
    
    gemmi_pkg -->|"imports"| gemmi_ext
    gemmi_cpp -->|"defines"| ext_def
    ext_def -->|"creates"| gemmi_ext
    common_h -->|"declares add_* functions"| gemmi_cpp
    init_py -->|"package entry"| gemmi_pkg
    stubs -->|"generated from"| gemmi_ext
```

Sources: [python/gemmi.cpp:159-165](), [python/common.h:27-48](), [CMakeLists.txt:29]()

### Extension Registration
The C++ extension `gemmi_ext` is initialized in `python/gemmi.cpp` using the `NB_MODULE` macro [python/gemmi.cpp:159](). An unusual setup is used where importing `gemmi_ext` adds classes and functions directly to the `gemmi` namespace [python/gemmi.cpp:160-162]().

The binding is modularized into several `add_*` functions (e.g., `add_cif`, `add_mtz`, `add_grid`) declared in `python/common.h` [python/common.h:27-48]() and implemented across various `.cpp` files in the `python/` directory.

## Verifying Installation

To verify the installation and check the version:

```python
import gemmi
print(gemmi.__version__)
```

The version string is sourced from `include/gemmi/version.hpp` [include/gemmi/version.hpp:8]() and exposed via `gemmi.__version__` in the extension module [python/gemmi.cpp:165]().

To run the comprehensive test suite:

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

Sources: [python/gemmi.cpp:165](), [run-tests.sh:52](), [include/gemmi/version.hpp:8]()

## Python Version and Platform Support

Gemmi uses `cibuildwheel` to generate wheels for a wide variety of environments [pyproject.toml:92-98]().

| Category | Supported / Configured Values |
|----------|-------------------------------|
| **Python** | >= 3.9 [pyproject.toml:13]() |
| **OS** | Ubuntu (22.04, 24.04), Windows 2022, macOS (14, 15) [.github/workflows/wheels2.yml:27]() |
| **Arch** | x86_64, arm64, Intel [.github/workflows/wheels2.yml:27]() |
| **Dependencies** | nanobind >= 2.4, scikit-build-core [pyproject.toml:1-6]() |

Sources: [pyproject.toml:1-13](), [.github/workflows/wheels2.yml:27]()

## Development and Advanced Configuration

Advanced build flags can be passed via `SKBUILD_CMAKE_ARGS` [pyproject.toml:98]():

- `FETCH_ZLIB_NG=ON`: Downloads and statically links `zlib-ng` for better performance [CMakeLists.txt:121-122]().
- `GENERATE_STUBS=ON`: Automatically creates `.pyi` files during the build [CMakeLists.txt:29]().
- `STANDALONE_PYTHON_MODULE=ON`: Avoids linking the Python module to a shared `libgemmi_cpp` library, simplifying distribution [CMakeLists.txt:32]().

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:29-32](), [pyproject.toml:98]()

This document provides an overview of the fundamental data structures in the Gemmi library, which forms the backbone of its crystallographic computing capabilities. These core data structures include macromolecular model representations, grid systems for volumetric data, crystallographic symmetry operations, and unit cell definitions.

## Structure Hierarchy

Gemmi uses a hierarchical organization for macromolecular structures that follows the standard PDB hierarchy.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Structure["gemmi::Structure"] {
        +std::string name
        +UnitCell cell
        +std::string spacegroup_hm
        +std::vector~Model~ models
        +std::vector~Entity~ entities
        +std::vector~Connection~ connections
        +first_model()
        +setup_entities()
    }
    
    class Model["gemmi::Model"] {
        +int num
        +std::vector~Chain~ chains
        +find_chain(name)
    }
    
    class Chain["gemmi::Chain"] {
        +std::string name
        +std::vector~Residue~ residues
        +get_polymer()
    }
    
    class Residue["gemmi::Residue"] {
        +std::string name
        +SeqId seqid
        +std::string subchain
        +std::string entity_id
        +EntityType entity_type
        +std::vector~Atom~ atoms
    }
    
    class Atom["gemmi::Atom"] {
        +std::string name
        +char altloc
        +Element element
        +Position pos
        +float occ
        +float b_iso
        +SMat33~float~ aniso
    }
    
    Structure "1" *-- "1..*" Model : contains
    Model "1" *-- "0..*" Chain : contains
    Chain "1" *-- "0..*" Residue : contains
    Residue "1" *-- "0..*" Atom : contains
```

The hierarchy starts with `Structure`, which contains multiple `Model` instances. Each `Model` contains `Chain` objects, each `Chain` contains `Residue` objects, and each `Residue` contains `Atom` objects. For details, see [Structure and Model System](#3.1).

### Structure
The top-level container representing a macromolecular structure [include/gemmi/model.hpp:882-1056](). It holds global information such as the unit cell, space group, and entity information.

### Model
Represents a single conformation of the structure [include/gemmi/model.hpp:718-868](). Multi-model files are common in NMR or ensembles.

### Chain
Represents a polymer chain, ligand, or water molecules [include/gemmi/model.hpp:482-610]().

### Residue
An amino acid, nucleotide, or ligand [include/gemmi/model.hpp:183-288](). It contains metadata like `entity_id` and `label_seq`.

### Atom
The basic unit containing coordinates (`pos`), occupancy (`occ`), and thermal parameters (`b_iso`, `aniso`) [include/gemmi/model.hpp:119-164]().

**Sources:** [include/gemmi/model.hpp:119-1056](), [docs/mol.rst:1-100]()

## Grid System

Gemmi's grid system handles 3D volumetric data such as electron density maps and masks.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class GridMeta["gemmi::GridMeta"] {
        +UnitCell unit_cell
        +const SpaceGroup* spacegroup
        +int nu, nv, nw
        +point_count()
    }
    
    class GridBase["gemmi::GridBase&lt;T&gt;"] {
        +std::vector~T~ data
    }
    
    class Grid["gemmi::Grid&lt;T&gt;"] {
        +interpolate_value()
        +get_value(u, v, w)
    }
    
    GridMeta <|-- GridBase : inherits
    GridBase <|-- Grid : inherits
```

The system is built on `GridMeta` (metadata), `GridBase` (data storage), and `Grid` (interpolation and logic). For details, see [Grid and Map System](#3.2).

**Sources:** [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:168-550]()

## Symmetry System

The symmetry system represents crystallographic symmetry operations and space groups.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Op["gemmi::Op"] {
        +Rot rot
        +Tran tran
        +inverse()
        +apply_to_xyz(xyz)
    }
    
    class GroupOps["gemmi::GroupOps"] {
        +std::vector~Op~ sym_ops
        +std::vector~Op::Tran~ cen_ops
        +is_centrosymmetric()
    }
    
    class SpaceGroup["gemmi::SpaceGroup"] {
        +int number
        +std::string hm
        +operations()
    }
    
    SpaceGroup --> GroupOps : provides
    GroupOps "1" o-- "1..*" Op : contains
```

### Op
Represents a symmetry operation using an integer rotation matrix and translation vector with a fixed denominator `DEN=24` [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:30-216]().

### GroupOps
A collection of `Op` objects representing a symmetry group [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:254-478]().

### SpaceGroup
High-level representation of a space group including symbols and lookup tables [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:1089-1184](). For details, see [Symmetry Operations](#3.3).

**Sources:** [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:30-1184](), [python/sym.cpp:15-150]()

## Unit Cell and Coordinates

Gemmi provides primitives for handling unit cell parameters and coordinate transformations.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Vec3["gemmi::Vec3"] {
        +double x, y, z
    }
    
    class Position["gemmi::Position"] {
        +Cartesian coordinates
    }
    
    class Fractional["gemmi::Fractional"] {
        +Fractional coordinates
        +wrap_to_unit()
    }
    
    class UnitCell["gemmi::UnitCell"] {
        +double a, b, c
        +Transform orth
        +Transform frac
        +orthogonalize(f)
        +fractionalize(p)
    }
    
    Vec3 <|-- Position : inherits
    Vec3 <|-- Fractional : inherits
    UnitCell o-- Position : uses
```

### UnitCell
Stores cell parameters and pre-calculated `Transform` matrices for converting between `Position` (orthogonal) and `Fractional` coordinates [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:165-374](). For details, see [Unit Cell and Coordinate Transformations](#3.4).

**Sources:** [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:32-374](), [include/gemmi/math.hpp:142-489]()

## Reflection Data

Reflection data is handled primarily through the `Mtz` class for binary files and `AsuData` for organized reciprocal space data. For details, see [Reflection Data](#3.5).

**Sources:** [include/gemmi/model.hpp:27-28](), [python/unitcell.cpp:103-180]()

# Structure and Model System

<details>

The Structure and Model System is the core component of Gemmi that represents macromolecular structures in memory. It provides a comprehensive, hierarchical data model for working with structural biology data, including proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, and solvent molecules.

## Structure Hierarchy Overview

The Structure and Model System is organized as a hierarchical data structure that reflects the standard organization of macromolecular structures:

### Data Entity Hierarchy
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Hierarchical Organization [include/gemmi/model.hpp]"
        Structure["Structure (class)"] --> Model["Model (class)"]
        Model --> Chain["Chain (class)"]
        Chain --> Residue["Residue (struct)"]
        Residue --> Atom["Atom (struct)"]
    end

    Structure -.- |"cell"| Cell["UnitCell"]
    Structure -.- |"entities"| Entities["EntityList"]
    Structure -.- |"connections"| Connections["ConnectionList"]
    Structure -.- |"assemblies"| Assemblies["AssemblyList"]
    Structure -.- |"ncs"| NCS["NcsOpList"]
```
Sources: [include/gemmi/model.hpp:136-1056](), [docs/mol.rst:1-27]()

This hierarchy mirrors the organization used in the PDB and mmCIF formats:

1.  **Structure**: The top-level container ([include/gemmi/model.hpp:883]()) representing a complete macromolecular structure.
2.  **Model**: Alternative models (e.g., NMR ensembles) ([include/gemmi/model.hpp:718]()).
3.  **Chain**: Distinct polymer chains or groups of water molecules ([include/gemmi/model.hpp:482]()).
4.  **Residue**: Individual residues or chemical components ([include/gemmi/model.hpp:200]()).
5.  **Atom**: Individual atoms with coordinates and properties ([include/gemmi/model.hpp:136]()).

## Alternative Conformations and Microheterogeneities

Gemmi handles alternative atom locations and microheterogeneities (point mutations) through the `altloc` field and specialized proxy objects.

### Conformer Logic
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Code Entities [include/gemmi/model.hpp]"
        Residue["Residue"] --> A1["Atom (altloc='A')"]
        Residue --> A2["Atom (altloc='B')"]
        ResGroup["ResidueGroup"] --> R1["Residue (name='SER')"]
        ResGroup --> R2["Residue (name='ALA')"]
    end
```
Sources: [include/gemmi/model.hpp:136-164](), [include/gemmi/model.hpp:423-440](), [docs/mol.rst:69-100]()

Gemmi provides three primary ways to handle these:
1.  **Manual Handling**: Access the `altloc` field directly in the `Atom` struct [include/gemmi/model.hpp:139]().
2.  **Filtering**: Use `remove_alternative_conformations()` to strip all but the first conformer [python/mol.cpp:5]().
3.  **Grouping**: Use `ResidueGroup` and `AtomGroup` proxy objects to iterate over sets of alternatives [include/gemmi/model.hpp:183-197]().

## Key Classes and Implementation

### Structure
The `Structure` class is the root container. It manages global metadata and structural data.
*   **Space Group & Cell**: Stores `UnitCell` and `SpaceGroup` info [include/gemmi/model.hpp:886-887]().
*   **Entities**: Managed via `entities` (vector of `Entity`) [include/gemmi/model.hpp:891]().
*   **Models**: Stored in a `std::vector<Model>` [include/gemmi/model.hpp:905]().

### Model
A `Model` represents one coordinate set.
*   **Subchains**: Implements `get_subchain()` to find residues by `label_asym_id` [include/gemmi/model.hpp:753]().
*   **Global Iteration**: `all()` returns a proxy for iterating over all atoms as `CRA` (Chain-Residue-Atom) triples [include/gemmi/model.hpp:852]().

### Residue
The `Residue` struct inherits from `ResidueId` [include/gemmi/model.hpp:200]().
*   **Metadata**: Stores `subchain` (`label_asym_id`), `entity_id`, and `label_seq` [include/gemmi/model.hpp:204-206]().
*   **Atoms**: Contains a `std::vector<Atom>` [include/gemmi/model.hpp:214]().

### Atom
The `Atom` struct is the leaf node [include/gemmi/model.hpp:136]().
*   **Properties**: Includes `pos` (`Position`), `occ` (occupancy), `b_iso`, and `aniso` (`SMat33<float>`) [include/gemmi/model.hpp:147-151]().
*   **Charge**: Stored as a `signed char` [include/gemmi/model.hpp:140]().

## Subchain and Entity System

Gemmi distinguishes between `auth_asym_id` (traditional PDB Chain ID) and `label_asym_id` (mmCIF Subchain ID).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "ID Mapping [include/gemmi/model.hpp]"
        Chain["Chain (name = auth_asym_id)"] --> Residue["Residue"]
        Residue --> SubID["subchain (label_asym_id)"]
        Residue --> EntID["entity_id"]
    end
    Structure --> EntityList["entities (std::vector<Entity>)"]
    EntityList --> Entity["Entity"]
    Entity --> EType["entity_type (Polymer/NonPolymer/Water)"]
```
Sources: [include/gemmi/model.hpp:467-480](), [include/gemmi/metadata.hpp:127-142](), [docs/mol.rst:15-27]()

The `setup_entities()` function is critical for populating these relationships from files that lack explicit entity categories [docs/mol.rst:151-164]().

## Selection and Navigation

The system supports complex selections via the `Selection` class [python/mol.cpp:84]().

### CRA (Chain-Residue-Atom)
The `CRA` struct provides a pointer-based reference to a specific atom within the hierarchy, allowing for efficient navigation without searching [python/mol.cpp:115-127]().

### Sequence ID (SeqId)
`SeqId` handles residue numbering, including insertion codes [include/gemmi/seqid.hpp](). It supports string parsing (e.g., "10A") and comparison [python/meta.cpp:28-44]().

## File I/O Integration

The model system is closely integrated with PDB and mmCIF parsers.

| Format | Reader Function | File Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **PDB** | `read_pdb_file()` | [include/gemmi/pdb.hpp:62]() |
| **mmCIF** | `make_structure_from_block()` | [include/gemmi/mmcif.hpp:18]() |
| **CCD** | `make_residue_from_chemcomp_block()` | [include/gemmi/mmcif.hpp:49]() |

### Output Options
*   **PdbWriteOptions**: Controls `TER` records, `SSBOND`, and `LINK` records [include/gemmi/to_pdb.hpp:13-30]().
*   **MmcifOutputGroups**: Toggles specific mmCIF categories during serialization [include/gemmi/to_mmcif.hpp:13-57]().

## Common Operations

### Modification Functions
*   **Renumbering**: `renumber_models()` [include/gemmi/mmcif.hpp:74]().
*   **Merging**: `merge_chain_parts()` joins discontinuous chain segments [include/gemmi/model.hpp:948]().
*   **Cleaning**: `remove_empty_children()` prunes the hierarchy [include/gemmi/model.hpp:126]().

### Calculation Functions
*   **B-factors**: `b_eq()` calculates equivalent isotropic B-factors from anisotropic tensors [include/gemmi/model.hpp:163]().
*   **Mass**: `calculate_mass()` (via `calculate.hpp`) [python/mol.cpp:4]().

Sources: [include/gemmi/model.hpp](), [python/mol.cpp](), [docs/mol.rst](), [include/gemmi/metadata.hpp]().

# Page: Grid and Map System

# Grid and Map System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The Grid and Map System in Gemmi provides functionality for handling 3D volumetric data, particularly electron density maps used in macromolecular crystallography and cryo-EM. This system enables storage, manipulation, and analysis of grid-based data with support for crystallographic symmetry and unit cell transformations. For handling reflection data, see [3.5 Reflection Data]().

## Core Data Structures

The Grid and Map System is built on a hierarchy of classes that provide increasingly specialized functionality. The system uses a Fortran-style contiguous data layout where the first index (u) changes fastest [docs/grid.rst:22-24]().

### Grid Entity Hierarchy

The following diagram maps the logical concepts of the volumetric system to their specific C++ class implementations.

Title: Grid System Entity Mapping
```mermaid
classDiagram
    class GridMeta {
        <<struct>>
        +UnitCell unit_cell
        +SpaceGroup* spacegroup
        +int nu, nv, nw
        +AxisOrder axis_order
        +point_count() size_t
        +get_fractional(int u, int v, int w) Fractional
        +get_position(int u, int v, int w) Position
    }
    class GridBase_T_ {
        <<struct>>
        +vector~T~ data
        +fill(T value) void
        +sum() T
    }
    class Grid_T_ {
        <<struct>>
        +double[3] spacing
        +set_size(int nu, int nv, int nw) void
        +set_size_from_spacing(double spacing, GridSizeRounding rounding) void
        +get_value(int u, int v, int w) T
        +set_value(int u, int v, int w, T x) void
        +interpolate_value(Position pos, int order) T
        +symmetrize_max() void
    }
    class Ccp4_T_ {
        <<struct>>
        +Grid~T~ grid
        +vector~int32_t~ ccp4_header
        +read_ccp4_file(string path) void
        +write_ccp4_map(string path) void
        +setup(double nan_replacement, MapSetup mode) void
    }
    GridMeta <|-- GridBase_T_
    GridBase_T_ <|-- Grid_T_
    Grid_T_ --* Ccp4_T_ : contains
```
Sources: [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:168-172](), [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:237-241](), [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:311-315](), [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp:242-246]()

### GridMeta
`GridMeta` is the base struct containing essential grid metadata including the `UnitCell`, `SpaceGroup`, and dimensions `nu`, `nv`, `nw` [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:168-172](). It handles the mapping of grid indices to fractional and orthogonal space [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:175-182]().

### GridBase<T>
`GridBase<T>` extends `GridMeta` with a `std::vector<T>` for data storage [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:237-241](). It defines the `Point` helper class which bundles coordinates with a pointer to the value [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:244-252]().

### Grid<T>
`Grid<T>` is the primary class for density manipulation. It adds `spacing` (precalculated distance between grid planes) [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:313]() and complex operations like interpolation and symmetry handling.

### Ccp4<T>
`Ccp4<T>` encapsulates a `Grid<T>` and the raw `ccp4_header` words [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp:242-246](). It provides the high-level API for reading and writing standard CCP4/MRC files [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp:360-490]().

## Coordinate Systems and Transformations

The system bridges discrete grid indices with physical space using the `UnitCell` [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:15]().

Title: Coordinate Space Flow
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Grid Space"
        IDX["Grid Indices (u, v, w)"]
    end
    subgraph "Crystallographic Space"
        FRAC["Fractional Coords (x, y, z)"]
    end
    subgraph "Physical Space"
        CART["Cartesian Coords (Å)"]
    end

    IDX -- "GridMeta::get_fractional()" --> FRAC
    FRAC -- "UnitCell::orthogonalize()" --> CART
    CART -- "UnitCell::fractionalize()" --> FRAC
    FRAC -- "Grid::get_nearest_point()" --> IDX
```
Sources: [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:176-182](), [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:412-426]()

## Creating and Setting Up Grids

### Size Determination
Grids can be sized manually via `set_size()` or automatically via `set_size_from_spacing()` [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:352-384](). The latter uses `good_grid_size()` to ensure the dimensions are:
1. Compatible with the `SpaceGroup` symmetry factors [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:104-112]().
2. "FFT-friendly" by having small prime factors (2, 3, 5) [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:45-52]().
3. Equal for symmetry-related directions [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:90-101]().

### From a Structure
The `setup_from<Structure>` method initializes grid dimensions and unit cell parameters directly from a molecular model [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:341-350]().

## Data Manipulation and Interpolation

### Access Methods
*   **Wrapping Access**: `get_value(u, v, w)` and `set_value(u, v, w, x)` use `modulo` to handle periodic boundary conditions (PBC) automatically [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:387-401]().
*   **Fast Access**: `index_q(u, v, w)` provides the fastest index calculation but assumes the point is within the primary unit cell [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:209-211]().

### Interpolation
Gemmi supports multiple interpolation orders [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:437-440]():
1.  **Order 0**: Nearest neighbor.
2.  **Order 1**: Trilinear interpolation [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:445-468]().
3.  **Order 3**: Tricubic interpolation using Catmull–Rom splines for smoother density representation [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:470-554]().

## Symmetry Operations

The `Grid` class can enforce crystallographic symmetry across the volume. If a `SpaceGroup` is assigned, `symmetrize_max()`, `symmetrize_min()`, `symmetrize_avg()`, and `symmetrize_sum()` iterate through all symmetry-equivalent positions to harmonize values [include/gemmi/grid.hpp:719-781]().

## Solvent Masking and Blobs

### Solvent Masking
The `SolventMasker` and associated functions in `solmask.hpp` generate masks based on atomic coordinates [include/gemmi/solmask.hpp:1-12]().
*   **Atomic Radii**: Supports various sets including `VanDerWaals`, `Cctbx`, and `Refmac` [include/gemmi/solmask.hpp:14]().
*   **mask_points_in_radius**: Marks all grid points within a specific radius of atoms in a `Model` [include/gemmi/solmask.hpp:107-129]().

### Blob Detection
The `find_blobs_by_flood_fill` function identifies connected regions of density above a certain threshold [include/gemmi/blob.hpp:26](). It returns a vector of `Blob` objects containing the centroid, peak position, and volume [python/grid.cpp:26-27]().

## CCP4 Map Format Handling

The `Ccp4` class handles the binary I/O for the CCP4/MRC map format [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp:3]().

| Feature | Description | Code Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Modes** | Supports Mode 0 (int8), 1 (int16), 2 (float32), 6 (uint16), and 12 (float16) | [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp:27-50](), [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp:413-430]() |
| **Axis Order** | Supports reordering axes to XYZ (standard) or ZYX | [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp:58-62](), [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp:113-124]() |
| **Header** | Provides methods to read/write specific header words (e.g., `header_i32(1)` for NX) | [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp:74-111]() |
| **Symmetry** | Reads/writes symmetry operations to the extended header | [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp:193-195]() |

Sources: [include/gemmi/ccp4.hpp:242-490]()

## Python Integration

Gemmi exposes grid functionality to Python via `FloatGrid` (for density) and `Int8Grid` (for masks) [docs/grid.rst:36-38]().

*   **NumPy Integration**: The `array` property provides a zero-copy NumPy view of the grid data [python/grid.cpp:61-65]().
*   **Flexible Interpolation**: `interpolate_position_array` allows batch interpolation of coordinate arrays using NumPy [python/grid.cpp:173-181]().
*   **Isosurface Extraction**: `extract_isosurface` implements the Marching Cubes algorithm to generate mesh data from the grid [python/grid.cpp:24-25]().

Sources: [python/grid.cpp:43-162](), [python/grid.cpp:217-255](), [docs/grid.rst:108-122]()

# Page: Symmetry Operations

# Symmetry Operations

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/code/sym.cpp](docs/code/sym.cpp)
- [docs/contents-help.txt](docs/contents-help.txt)
- [docs/sg-help.txt](docs/sg-help.txt)

- [include/gemmi/atof.hpp](include/gemmi/atof.hpp)
- [include/gemmi/atox.hpp](include/gemmi/atox.hpp)
- [include/gemmi/recgrid.hpp](include/gemmi/recgrid.hpp)
- [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp](include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp)
- [include/gemmi/third_party/pocketfft_hdronly.h](include/gemmi/third_party/pocketfft_hdronly.h)
- [python/recgrid.cpp](python/recgrid.cpp)

- [src/symmetry.cpp](src/symmetry.cpp)
- [tests/test_symmetry.py](tests/test_symmetry.py)

</details>



This page covers crystallographic symmetry operations in the Gemmi library, explaining their representation, manipulation, and application. Symmetry operations define how coordinates and Miller indices transform in a crystal.

## 1. Symmetry Representation: The Op Class

Gemmi represents a single symmetry operation (or a change-of-basis transformation) using the `Op` struct. It consists of a $3 \times 3$ rotation matrix and a translation vector.

### Internal Data Structure
To avoid floating-point issues, Gemmi uses integer arithmetic with a fixed denominator `DEN = 24`. This denominator is chosen because it is a multiple of 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, and 12, allowing exact representation of all standard crystallographic translations and change-of-basis operations [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:31-33]().

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Op {
        +static int DEN = 24
        +Rot rot
        +Tran tran
        +char notation
        +triplet(style) string
        +inverse() Op
        +combine(Op) Op
        +apply_to_xyz(array) array
        +apply_to_hkl(Miller) Miller
        +phase_shift(Miller) double
    }
    class Rot {
        +int[3][3] data
    }
    class Tran {
        +int[3] data
    }
    Op *-- Rot
    Op *-- Tran
```

- **`rot`**: A $3 \times 3$ array of integers. The actual rotation matrix is $rot / DEN$ [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:35]().
- **`tran`**: An array of 3 integers. The actual translation is $tran / DEN$ [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:36]().
- **`notation`**: A flag identifying the coordinate system. `'x'` denotes real space (XYZ), while `'h'` denotes reciprocal space (HKL) [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:37-39]().

Sources: [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:30-46](), [python/sym.cpp:25-46]()

## 2. Parsing and Generation

Symmetry operations are most commonly instantiated from coordinate triplets or Seitz matrices.

### Coordinate Triplets
The `parse_triplet` function converts strings like `"x, y+1/2, -z"` into an `Op` object [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:109-129](). It handles:
- Fractions (e.g., `1/2`, `2/3`).
- Decimal fractions found in some CIF files (e.g., `0.5-x`) [src/symmetry.cpp:59-65]().
- Different notations: `x,y,z`, `h,k,l`, or `a,b,c` [src/symmetry.cpp:180-188]().

### Seitz Matrices
Gemmi can convert to and from 4x4 Seitz matrices, which combine rotation and translation into a single affine transformation matrix [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:159-174]().

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    String["'x, y+1/2, -z'"] -- "parse_triplet()" --> OpObj["Op Object"]
    Seitz["4x4 Matrix"] -- "seitz_to_op()" --> OpObj
    OpObj -- "int_seitz()" --> Seitz
    OpObj -- "triplet()" --> String
```

Sources: [src/symmetry.cpp:20-129](), [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:159-174](), [python/sym.cpp:49-68]()

## 3. Group Operations: GroupOps

The `GroupOps` class represents a symmetry group, typically associated with a space group. It explicitly separates centering vectors from general symmetry operations to optimize calculations [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:254-260]().

### Class Structure
- **`sym_ops`**: A vector of `Op` objects representing the site-symmetry operations [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:261]().
- **`cen_ops`**: A vector of `Tran` (integer triplets) representing lattice centering (e.g., $(1/2, 1/2, 1/2)$ for I-centering) [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:262]().

### Key Group Functions
| Function | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `order()` | Returns the total number of operations ($sym\_ops.size() \times cen\_ops.size()$) [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:269](). |
| `is_centrosymmetric()` | Checks if the group contains an inversion center [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:309](). |
| `is_systematically_absent(hkl)` | Determines if a reflection is absent due to glide planes or screw axes [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:371](). |
| `epsilon_factor(hkl)` | Calculates the epsilon factor (statistical weight) for a reflection [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:359](). |

Sources: [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:254-389](), [python/sym.cpp:94-139]()

## 4. Space Groups and Hall Symbols

Gemmi includes an extensive table of space group settings (560+ entries) derived from CCP4's `syminfo.lib` and `sgtbx` [docs/symmetry.rst:9-26]().

### SpaceGroup Lookup
Space groups can be retrieved by:
1. **Name/H-M Symbol**: `find_spacegroup_by_name("P 21 21 21")` [docs/symmetry.rst:60-71]().
2. **Number**: `find_spacegroup_by_number(19)` [docs/symmetry.rst:128-133]().
3. **Operations**: `find_spacegroup_by_ops(group_ops)` [docs/symmetry.rst:161-165]().

### Hall Symbols
Hall symbols provide a concise, unambiguous way to generate all symmetry operations of a group. Gemmi uses `generators_from_hall` to parse these symbols into `GroupOps` [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:510-520]().

Sources: [docs/symmetry.rst:6-187](), [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:477-510]()

## 5. Reciprocal Space Operations

### Reciprocal ASU (Asymmetric Unit)
The `ReciprocalAsu` class defines the boundaries of the asymmetric unit in reciprocal space. It is used to reduce any Miller index $H$ to its representative index $H_{asu}$ in the primary ASU [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:713-720]().

- **`is_in(hkl)`**: Checks if a reflection is within the ASU [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:725]().
- **`to_asu(hkl, gops)`**: Returns the representative HKL and the symmetry operation index used to reach it [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:734]().

### Phase Shifts and Twinning
When a symmetry operation is applied to a reflection, it may introduce a phase shift $\Delta\phi = -2\pi (h \cdot t)$ [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:154-157]().
For twinning, Gemmi provides `Twinning` structures to handle twin laws (symmetry operations relating different domains) and calculate twin fractions [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:814-830]().

Sources: [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:713-810](), [include/gemmi/asudata.hpp:156-168]()

## 6. Implementation and Data Flow

The following diagram illustrates how symmetry data flows from raw input (triplets/symbols) to the application on structural data.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Input: Hall Symbol / Triplets"] -- "parse_triplet() / generators_from_hall()" --> OpGroup["GroupOps (sym_ops + cen_ops)"]
    OpGroup -- "is_systematically_absent()" --> Filter["Reflection Filter"]
    OpGroup -- "apply_to_xyz()" --> AtomPos["Symmetry-Equivalent Atoms"]
    
    SpaceGroupTable["SpaceGroup Table (560+ settings)"] -- "operations()" --> OpGroup
    
    subgraph GridOps["Grid Operations"]
        OpGroup -- "get_scaled_ops()" --> ScaledOps["GridOp (Integer-only)"]
    end
    
    ScaledOps -- "apply(u, v, w)" --> GridIndices["Grid Index Mapping"]
```

Sources: [include/gemmi/symmetry.hpp:254-308](), [include/gemmi/asumask.hpp:83-107](), [docs/symmetry.rst:55-71]()

# Unit Cell and Coordinate Transformations

This page documents the fundamental components within GEMMI for working with unit cells and coordinate transformations in crystallography. It covers the representation of unit cells, conversion between coordinate systems, distance calculations with periodic boundary conditions, lattice reduction, and mathematical primitives.

## Core Concepts and Class Architecture

In crystallography, a unit cell is defined by its parameters (lengths a, b, c and angles α, β, γ) and provides the foundation for crystal structure representation. GEMMI implements this through the `UnitCell` class and related coordinate systems.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class UnitCellParameters {
        +double a, b, c
        +double alpha, beta, gamma
        +approx()
    }
    
    class UnitCell {
        +Transform orth
        +Transform frac
        +double volume
        +double ar, br, cr
        +vector~FTransform~ images
        +orthogonalize()
        +fractionalize()
        +distance_sq()
        +find_nearest_image()
        +is_crystal()
    }
    
    class Vec3_ {
        +Real x, y, z
        +dot()
        +cross()
        +length()
    }
    
    class Position {
        +inherits Vec3
    }
    
    class Fractional {
        +inherits Vec3
        +wrap_to_unit()
        +wrap_to_zero()
    }
    
    class Transform {
        +Mat33 mat
        +Vec3 vec
        +apply()
        +combine()
        +inverse()
    }
    
    class Mat33 {
        +double[3][3] a
        +multiply()
        +inverse()
        +determinant()
    }

    class SMat33 {
        +u11, u22, u33, u12, u13, u23
        +calculate_eigenvalues()
        +inverse()
    }
    
    UnitCellParameters <|-- UnitCell
    Vec3_ <|-- Position
    Vec3_ <|-- Fractional
    Transform <|-- FTransform
    UnitCell -- Transform : contains
    Transform -- Mat33 : contains
    SMat33 -- Mat33 : as_mat33()
```

Sources: [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:137-165](), [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:32-45](), [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:50-74](), [include/gemmi/math.hpp:58-114](), [include/gemmi/math.hpp:130-245](), [include/gemmi/math.hpp:393-420](), [include/gemmi/math.hpp:422-550]()

## Mathematical Primitives

GEMMI relies on several low-level mathematical structures for 3D linear algebra:

*   **`Vec3` / `Vec3f`**: Template-based 3D vectors (double and float versions). Includes standard operations like `dot()`, `cross()`, and `length()`. [include/gemmi/math.hpp:58-118]()
*   **`Mat33`**: A 3x3 matrix primarily used for rotation and orthogonalization. Supports matrix multiplication (`multiply()`), inversion (`inverse()`), and determinant calculation. [include/gemmi/math.hpp:130-245]()
*   **`SMat33`**: A symmetric 3x3 matrix, efficient for storing Atomic Displacement Parameters (ADPs) or metric tensors. It provides `calculate_eigenvalues()` using a closed-form solution for 3x3 symmetric matrices. [include/gemmi/math.hpp:422-550]()
*   **`Transform`**: Combines a `Mat33` (rotation/scaling) and a `Vec3` (translation). [include/gemmi/math.hpp:393-420]()

Sources: [include/gemmi/math.hpp:58-550]()

## Coordinate Systems

Crystallography uses two primary coordinate systems represented by specialized classes inheriting from `Vec3`:

1.  **Fractional Coordinates** (`Fractional` class): Positions expressed as fractions of unit cell dimensions. Includes utility methods like `wrap_to_unit()` (shifts coordinates into the [0, 1) range). [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:50-74]()
2.  **Orthogonal Coordinates** (`Position` class): Cartesian coordinates in Ångstroms. [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:32-45]()

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        NC["Non-crystalline / NMR"]
        CR["Crystal Lattice"]
        FR["Fractional Space"]
        OR["Orthogonal Space"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        UC["UnitCell::is_crystal()"]
        FRC["Fractional struct"]
        POS["Position struct"]
        ORTH["UnitCell::orthogonalize()"]
        FRAC["UnitCell::fractionalize()"]
    end
    
    NC --> UC
    CR --> UC
    FR --> FRC
    OR --> POS
    FRC -- ORTH --> POS
    POS -- FRAC --> FRC
```

Sources: [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:32-74](), [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:187-187](), [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:391-407]()

## Unit Cell Initialization and Properties

A `UnitCell` is initialized with six parameters: $a, b, c, \alpha, \beta, \gamma$. [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:167-171]()

| Property | Description | Implementation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `volume` | Unit cell volume in Å³ | [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:208-211]() |
| `orth` | Orthogonalization `Transform` | [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:232-234]() |
| `frac` | Fractionalization `Transform` | [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:241-243]() |
| `ar, br, cr` | Reciprocal cell dimensions $a^*, b^*, c^*$ | [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:214-216]() |
| `is_crystal()` | Checks if cell is not a dummy 1x1x1 cell | [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:187-187]() |

The orthogonalization follows the Niggli-it (or PDB) convention where the $a$-axis is collinear with the Cartesian $x$-axis. [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:223-234]()

Sources: [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:165-245]()

## Periodic Boundary Conditions and Nearest Images

GEMMI handles the periodic nature of crystals through "minimum image" conventions.

*   **`distance_sq(pos1, pos2)`**: Calculates the squared distance between two points, accounting for periodic boundary conditions by finding the closest periodic image. [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:433-439]()
*   **`find_nearest_image()`**: Returns a `NearestImage` object containing the shortest distance, the symmetry operation used, and the periodic shift ($n_a, n_b, n_c$). [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:446-508]()
*   **`wrap_to_unit()`**: Shifts a `Fractional` coordinate by integers so that $0 \le x, y, z < 1$. [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:60-62]()

### NearestImage Structure
```cpp
struct NearestImage {
  double dist_sq;
  int pbc_shift[3]; // integer shifts along cell axes
  int sym_idx;      // index into UnitCell::images
  std::string symmetry_code(bool underscore); // e.g., "1_555"
};
```
Sources: [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:79-108](), [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:446-508]()

## Lattice Reduction and Twinning

GEMMI includes tools for lattice analysis, primarily located in `cellred.hpp` and `twin.hpp`.

*   **Niggli Reduction**: Implemented via `NiggliReduction` (referenced in `cellred.hpp`) to find a unique, standardized primitive cell. [include/gemmi/cellred.hpp:1-15]()
*   **Selling-Delaunay Reduction**: Used for lattice characterization.
*   **Twinning**: `find_lattice_2fold_ops()` identifies potential twin laws by searching for 2-fold operations that approximately map the lattice to itself within a given `max_obliq` (obliquity) tolerance. [include/gemmi/twin.hpp:147-150]()

Sources: [include/gemmi/twin.hpp:147-153](), [include/gemmi/cellred.hpp:1-15]()

## Miller Indices and Resolution

The `UnitCell` class maps Miller indices ($h, k, l$) to reciprocal space distances:

*   **`calculate_1_d2(hkl)`**: Calculates $1/d^2 = 4(\sin \theta / \lambda)^2$. [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:565-573]()
*   **`calculate_d(hkl)`**: Calculates the resolution $d$ in Ångstroms. [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:575-578]()
*   **`get_hkl_limits(dmin)`**: Returns the maximum $h, k, l$ indices possible for a given resolution limit. [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:600-607]()

Sources: [include/gemmi/unitcell.hpp:565-607]()

## Python Bindings

The Python API exposes these mathematical primitives and unit cell operations with NumPy integration.

```python
import gemmi
import numpy as np

cell = gemmi.UnitCell(50, 60, 70, 90, 90, 90)
# Convert to numpy array
mat = np.array(cell.orth.mat) 

# Distance with PBC
d2 = cell.distance_sq(gemmi.Position(1,1,1), gemmi.Position(49,59,69))
```

Sources: [python/unitcell.cpp:103-183](), [python/unitcell.cpp:259-341]()

# Page: Reflection Data

# Reflection Data
